title: C4 Neutron Star

summary: A neutron star at the table centre pulls every ship and ordnance marker towards it at the start of every player turn, after special orders but before normal movement: Battleship 1D6, Cruiser 2D6, Escort 3D6, Ordnance 3D6, Defence 3D6, All Ahead Full +1D6, Burn Retros -1D6. Touching the star destroys the object (ships explode as Catastrophic result 12). A mysterious wreck worth 450 VP is pulled 2D6 closer each turn.
special_rules: Neutron Star gravity pull
Mysterious Wreck (450 VP) salvaged like C3's wrecks
Star base blocks line of sight
xr_dependencies: s.7 All Ahead Full / Burn Retros

xr_conflicts.source_text: Sub-plots are not active, no matter the reason. ... To avoid mathematical and miserable victories by disengage, the You COWARDS! rule grants: a 1000 VP bonus on turn 2 if there are no enemy ships left
xr_conflicts.xr_text: Each non-crippled capital ship, escort squadron, and defence installation that has disengaged before the end of the game awards the opposing player a number of victory points equal to 10% of that unit/squadron's total points value
xr_conflicts.effect: The pack's VP-to-Battle-Point table, 1250 or 1500pt limit, no sub-plots and the You COWARDS! bonus are a tournament layer. Outside a tournament the supplement would drop or keep them by decision.

xr_conflicts.source_text: At the start of every player turn, after Special Orders are attempted, but before normal movement commences, roll on the chart below ... directly towards the neutron star without changing your heading
xr_conflicts.xr_text: While in high orbit, ships do not need to move ... a ship may make a free turn when it begins and/or ends its move in high orbit
xr_conflicts.effect: New mechanic, no XR equivalent.

xr_conflicts.source_text: To recover the wreck, simply make contact with its base and declare you will attempt to recover it. Then roll a D6
xr_conflicts.xr_text: Drifting and blazing hulks cannot be ... boarded
xr_conflicts.effect: As in C3.

xr_conflicts: Checked: attack rating deployment, first turn, 8 turns.
missing_or_unclear: Whether the pull applies to every escort in a squadron by squadron roll or separately.
Size of the neutron star base.
'1 wreck set up 36cm away from the neutron star parallel to the long table edge': which direction.
notes: Printed table read from the page text: Battleship 1D6, Cruiser 2D6, Escort 3D6, Ordnance 3D6, Defense 3D6, All Ahead Full +1D6, Burn Retros -1D6.

group: BFG Tournament Mission Pack (AdeptiCon 2007-2010; booklet by Paolo Barbero)
title: C5 Shepard Moon
author: AdeptiCon 2010 (Mission 2)
summary: Two rings cross the table; a shepherd moon (a small planetoid) can be boarded like a ship. After boarding, roll a D6: 1 Tyranid infestation (D6 boarding torpedoes), 2-3 D6 robotic Eldar fighters, 4-5 D6 robotic Eldar bombers, 6 the moon becomes a Kroot Warsphere. Controlling it is worth 345 VP and the result cannot be taken back.
special_rules: Shepherd Moon boarding table
Control worth 345 VP
xr_dependencies: Eldar MMS v2.0 fighters and bombers

group: BFG Tournament Mission Pack (AdeptiCon 2007-2010; booklet by Paolo Barbero)
title: C6 Hide n' Seek
author: AdeptiCon 2010 (Mission 2)
summary: An anomaly sits at the centre of a dense asteroid field area. At the end of each player's movement phase, ships with line of sight to its centre suffer a Leadership penalty: -3 within 10cm, -2 within 30cm, -1 beyond. Asteroid fields block line of sight to the anomaly.
special_rules: Anomaly Leadership penalty by range
Majority ruling for escort squadrons partly in cover
